data.body:
S2 RESUMED after coordinator go-ahead, with time pressure to land S2 before RP-04 S7.3.a (insincere-illogical-antlion) starts its reconciler-engine cutover. Rebased onto origin/main 47c5626f8b (three new commits: argparse CLI parsing, RP-04 C3b store/io seam, RP-04 C3c cli/commands seam); both config gates verified green on that base; registry rows for binding_store.py now at config_ownership_exceptions.py lines 146-153.
S2 story brainy-cooked-hog: review-plan PASS signed, claimed, and file_impact extended to 8 paths to add scripts/config_ownership_exceptions.py per the coordinator directive.
S2 T1 dermatoid-brassy-junco took THREE review-plan rounds, each surfacing a real plan defect rather than noise:
(1) BLOCK - the extraction seam runs through note_absent_or_rekey, whose non-rekey branches call note_absent -> _retire, which the plan puts OUT of scope, and the plan never said how to split one method. REMEDIATED by documenting the four-step structure and specifying that ONLY step 4 (the re-key mutation) moves, while note_absent_or_rekey stays on the facade as coordinator and keeps the absence fall-through until T2. Also enumerated AC3's vague 'existing permitted cases' for stale-reverse removal as four concrete cases (bind_confirm rebind, unbind keyed pop + orphan sweep, re-key swap, _retire pop).
(2) BLOCK - the plan asserted preserving an EXISTING 'safety-abort on ambiguous double bind' that DOES NOT EXIST. Verified independently: bind_confirm unconditionally overwrites jira_key and pops the old reverse key only when it differs; a search for ambiguous/double-bind/safety-abort across binding_store.py, binding_repository.py and peer_state.py returns nothing, and there is no raise or abort in bind_confirm/unbind/rekey. REMEDIATED by correcting AC2 to the invariant that is real and testable - last-writer-wins with exactly one targeted reverse pop, no sweep, no ambiguity detection, no abort - and stating that adding an abort would be a forbidden behavior change needing its own ticket.
(3) BLOCK - leaf now contradicted PARENT S2 AC1, which carried the same aspirational 'safety-aborts ambiguous double binds' claim. REMEDIATED at the parent: corrected fc1c AC1 to the same narrower invariant and recorded why, which staled and required re-earning S2's own attestation (re-reviewed: PASS signed). Reserved the term 'safety-abort' for S3's interrupted-retirement completion, where it IS new behavior, so the tree carries one meaning. T1 then PASSED signed with only a P6 0.40 advisory.
This is the plan-review gate doing exactly its job: the decomposition had inherited a behavior claim that the code never implemented, and building to it would have introduced an unrequested behavior change into a pure-extraction slice.
S2 T1 CLAIMED. Oracle authored: 24 direct tests in state/test_binding_lifecycle.py against a signature-only scaffold - 18 RED with NotImplementedError plus 6 facade characterization tests green BY DESIGN (a refactor must not move the public contract, so those cannot be RED-first; their teeth come from mutation). 11 discriminators held out of the worktree to /tmp/rp02-heldout/S2T1_FULL.py: reverse-index cleanup semantics (rebind single-pop, unbind orphan sweep, keyless-entry sweep), the re-key both-index swap with absence reset, lifecycle-mutates-repo-dicts-not-copies, unknown-field survival, the keyed-pending sub-state, and all four facade rekey fall-through cases. 12 visible to the implementer plus the whole ~3250-test suite as regression oracle. NOTE: T1 does NOT move _env_int or the RECONCILER_ABSENT_RETIRE_GRACE read - those serve note_absent, which is T2 scope - so the config_ownership_exceptions.py re-registration lands in T2, not here.
